public_health_question.v: Did outpatient COVID-19 treatment, especially Paxlovid, differ by race and ethnicity among adult COVID-19 patients seeking care in January–July 2022?

ev.q: treatment with Paxlovid, Lagevrio, Veklury, and mAbs was assessed by race and ethnicity, overall and among high-risk patient groups
Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Outpatient Treatment of COVID-19
Using electronic health record (EHR) data from 692,570 COVID-19 patients aged ≥20 years who sought medical care during January–July 2022
This study used EHR data from 30 sites (each representing one or more health care systems) participating in PCORnet

equity.level_reason: Racial and ethnic disparities in Paxlovid treatment are framed, quantified as absolute and relative differences (35.8% lower for Black patients) and interpreted; access to treatment facilities, racism, implicit bias, transportation and language barriers are named as explanations.

level_alternative.reason: Determinants are offered as possible explanations in the Discussion, not measured or analyzed.

ev.q: Racial and ethnic disparities persisted in outpatient COVID-19 treatment through July 2022.
Disparities for Black, multiple or other race, and Hispanic patients were present across all age strata

racism and implicit biases among health care providers might have contributed to treatment disparities
lack of internet access for telemedicine services ( 6 ), limited transportation, and language barriers

equity.equity_measurement: Referents are White race and non-Hispanic ethnicity; race and ethnicity assessed separately (combined only for full period); AIAN and NHOPI collapsed; missing race/ethnicity excluded from contrasts; no adjustment possible with aggregate data.

ev.q: Paxlovid treatment was 24.9%, 23.1%, and 19.4% lower among multiple or other race, AIAN/NHOPI, and Asian patients, respectively, than among White patients
the percentage of patients aged 20–49, 50–64, 65–79, and ≥80 years who were prescribed Paxlovid was 20.9%, 34.3%, 39.9%, and 30.7%, respectively

notes: Design not named; cross-sectional inferred from aggregate EHR query. Headline contrasts are pairwise per dimension, but five race groups are each compared with White, so framework recorded as group. Immunocompromise and other-medication results are in supplementary tables only.
